open_points.subject: ownership boundary between service_api and instance_lifecycle
open_points.text: The service API's transport for the four services (R0-27, R0-28)
open_points.question: Does `service_api` own only the application-level service protocol, or does it own part of the HTTP transport that the listener is also said to own?
options: `instance_lifecycle` owns all HTTP transport; `service_api` owns authentication extraction, operation dispatch and application payload serialization
`service_api` owns the service HTTP adapter while `instance_lifecycle` owns only sockets and connection lifetime
The two modules jointly own the transport through a separately owned HTTP abstraction
open_points.default_guess: `instance_lifecycle` owns sockets and HTTP syntax/framing; `service_api` owns the service protocol after syntactic HTTP parsing.

open_points.subject: framed request boundary record
open_points.text: each request's body handed on as a stream that ends where HTTP's own framing ends the body
open_points.question: Which module owns the request object and stream contract passed from the listener to `service_api` or `owner_interface`, including the request target, parsed headers, duplicate-header representation, framing metadata, read errors and cancellation?
options: An `instance_lifecycle`-owned framed-request type
A shared model or interface owned by `models`
Separate input contracts owned by `service_api` and `owner_interface`
A concrete HTTP-library request object passed through directly
open_points.default_guess: Use an `instance_lifecycle`-owned immutable framed-request interface and a bounded body stream; surface modules receive it without depending on the HTTP library.

open_points.subject: HTTP response boundary
open_points.text:
The reading and writing of its wire format. The HTTP server, its
connections and HTTP's framing are `instance_lifecycle`'s listener's, as for
the owner interface.
open_points.question: What does a surface return to the listener, and which module chooses and writes HTTP response headers, body framing, connection headers and the final close or reuse decision?
options: The surface returns status, application headers and body bytes; the listener adds and writes HTTP framing
The surface writes directly to a listener-owned response stream
The listener owns the complete HTTP response, and the surface returns only a domain result
open_points.default_guess: The surface returns a status, permitted application headers and serialized body; `instance_lifecycle` adds HTTP framing and writes it to the connection.

open_points.subject: owner-session arrival versus rejection before a surface
open_points.text:
a request whose `Content-Length` or chunked framing is
malformed, or whose body ends before its framing says, is refused by the
listener, its connection closed, and reaches no surface
open_points.question: If an owner upload's head has been read while its session is valid but malformed chunking or premature EOF is discovered later, did the request reach the owner interface and restart the session's idle period as A13 rule 2 requires, or did it reach no surface and leave the session untouched?
options: Arrival at the multipart head reaches the owner-session check and restarts the idle period even if later body framing fails
The listener validates the complete framed body first, so the malformed request never reaches the owner-session check and does not restart the idle period
The listener records the A13 arrival effect itself without invoking the owner interface
open_points.default_guess: Honor A13's precise arrival rule: run the owner-session check when the upload head arrives and restart the idle period; replace “reaches no surface” with a narrower promise that malformed framing reaches no operation or store change.

witness.initial: An owner session is one second short of its 30-minute idle limit and holds no pending upload.
events: The owner sends a valid session cookie, CSRF field and multipart head before the idle limit.
The listener reads that head, then later encounters malformed chunk framing or EOF before the declared body end.
After the original idle limit, the owner sends another request using the same session.
outcomes: Under A13 rule 2, the upload arrived when its head was read, passed the session check and restarted the idle period, so the later request is accepted.
Under the changed State 3 clause, the malformed request reached no surface and could not perform the owner-session arrival effect, so the later request is refused as idle.
witness.observer: The owner, through whether the next owner-interface request is accepted or asks for sign-in.

open_points.subject: streaming upload limit versus prevalidation of framing
open_points.text:
a request whose `Content-Length` or chunked framing is
malformed, or whose body ends before its framing says, is refused by the
listener, its connection closed, and reaches no surface
open_points.question: For a chunked multipart upload with no trustworthy total length, must the listener buffer and validate the whole body before routing it, or may the owner interface consume the stream and enforce A19's file-part limit before later framing errors are known?
options: Buffer and validate the entire HTTP body before any surface receives it
Stream to the owner interface, enforcing the file-part limit immediately, even though a later framing error means the request already reached a surface
Make the listener parse multipart data and enforce the file-part limit while prevalidating the HTTP body
open_points.default_guess: Stream to the owner interface and enforce A19 at the first file byte over the limit; a later framing failure closes the connection and prevents operation completion, but cannot truthfully be said to have reached no surface.

witness.initial: A valid owner session sends a chunked multipart upload with no declared total length; its file part will exceed 50 MiB and a later chunk is malformed.
events: The listener receives valid framing through the first 50 MiB plus one byte of the file part.
The sender continues, then sends malformed chunk framing.
outcomes: A19 requires refusal as soon as Registry holds the first file byte over 50 MiB, so the owner-interface upload reader has already consumed the request before the later framing error.
The changed State 3 clause requires detecting the later framing error before the request reaches any surface, so the listener must retain or parse more of the body before the A19 refusal point.
witness.observer: The sender sees when the connection is refused, and the operator can observe whether Registry buffers data beyond the file limit.

open_points.subject: malformed HTTP framing predicate
open_points.text:
a request whose `Content-Length` or chunked framing is
malformed
open_points.question: Exactly which framing combinations are malformed, including duplicate `Content-Length` fields, conflicting equal or unequal lengths, simultaneous `Transfer-Encoding` and `Content-Length`, unsupported transfer codings, invalid chunk extensions and invalid or forbidden trailers?
options: Apply a named HTTP version and its framing rules strictly, rejecting every ambiguous combination
Accept combinations the chosen HTTP library normalizes safely
Declare an explicit closed set of accepted framing forms and reject everything else
open_points.default_guess: Support HTTP/1.1 framing strictly, reject `Transfer-Encoding` together with `Content-Length`, reject conflicting or syntactically invalid lengths, accept only final `chunked`, and validate chunk syntax and trailers.

open_points.subject: observable refusal for malformed framing
open_points.text:
is refused by the
listener, its connection closed
open_points.question: Before closing the connection, does the listener send an HTTP error response, and if so which status and body; or is malformed framing always rejected by a silent close?
options: Send a fixed HTTP 400 response and then close whenever a response can safely be written
Close silently without an HTTP response
Use different outcomes for malformed headers, malformed chunks and premature EOF
open_points.default_guess: Send a fixed empty HTTP 400 response and close when possible; use a silent close only when the connection cannot carry a response.

witness.initial: A client has an open connection to either surface.
events: The client sends a request with an invalid `Content-Length` value.
The listener detects the malformed framing and closes the connection.
outcomes: The listener first sends an HTTP 400 response and then closes.
The listener closes without sending any response bytes.
witness.observer: The HTTP client sees either a status response or only an EOF/reset.

open_points.subject: connection persistence and request sequencing
open_points.text:
The HTTP server, its
connections and HTTP's framing are `instance_lifecycle`'s listener's
open_points.question: After a valid response, does the listener close the connection or support persistent connections, and if persistent, may it read or process pipelined requests before the preceding response completes?
options: Close after every response
Support sequential HTTP/1.1 keep-alive but no concurrent pipelining
Support pipelining with responses kept in request order
open_points.default_guess: Support sequential HTTP/1.1 keep-alive, process one request at a time per connection, and close when either side requests it or framing requires it.

witness.initial: A client opens one connection and sends two valid requests without waiting for the first response.
events: The listener finishes reading the first request.
The second request is already present on the connection.
outcomes: The listener processes both requests on the persistent connection in order.
The listener answers the first request and closes, so the second request is not processed.
witness.observer: The client sees either two responses on one connection or must reconnect and resend the second request.

open_points.subject: supported HTTP protocol versions
open_points.text:
HTTP's framing of every request of both surfaces, one
implementation
open_points.question: Which HTTP versions and request forms does the one listener implementation accept, and what happens when a client uses another version?
options: HTTP/1.1 only
HTTP/1.0 and HTTP/1.1
HTTP/1.1 plus HTTP/2 through the same listener
open_points.default_guess: Accept HTTP/1.1 only and reject unsupported versions with a fixed version error followed by connection close.
